_comment: Branch protection policy for main. Applied by an administrator via scripts/apply-branch-protection.sh; CI never mutates it. See docs/dev/branch-protection.md for rationale. Four required contexts, each a name that does not change when CI changes: CI Gate is the ci.yml job `ci_gate`, which needs every ci.yml job that blocks main and runs scripts/ci_gate.py over their results (a skip is accepted only where the job's own `if:` was false; failure and cancellation are always red), so which jobs block main is the `needs:` list in ci.yml and the table in that script, changed in a reviewed pull request and never on this rule. Check Workflow Action Pins is required on its own, not only through the gate: it runs scripts/check-merge-group-triggers.py, which pins the gate's wiring and holds its `needs:` equal to the script's table, and a malformed gate that reported a skip could otherwise hide that validator's red. GQ Logic Tests and Fix Regression Gate are their own workflows and keep their own names. .github/CODEOWNERS is advisory, require_code_owner_reviews stays false and no approvals are required, so the four contexts are the gate. The format fence, the RustFS S3 suite and the Azurite suite run on pull requests as reporting contexts and again after merge. A red main branch is stop-the-line until fixed or reverted. Every merge into main goes through the merge queue with the squash method; the branch-protection endpoint this file drives has no field for the queue, so it is set on the rule page and checked there after every apply. Each required context's workflow also runs on merge_group (scripts/check-merge-group-triggers.py enforces it); Fix Regression Gate's merge-group run reports a pass without a check. No administrator bypass: enforce_admins is true.
